outcome_detail: Doe 1 v. McKnight, 1:24-cv-00217 (E.D. Mo.), filed November 21, 2024, remains open; additional Jane Doe/Mary Roe plaintiffs' claims (also naming the Missouri State Highway Patrol) were consolidated into the case. As of a June 12, 2026 amended case management order, a jury trial is set for September 29-30, 2026, with a pretrial conference on September 9, 2026. No settlement or judgment reported as of July 2026.
criminal_detail: David McKnight pleaded guilty in December 2025 in the U.S. District Court in Cape Girardeau to nine counts of deprivation of rights under color of law (unreasonable search and seizure) for searching nine women's cell phones without a warrant between September 12, 2023 and July 30, 2024. On April 28, 2026 he was sentenced to 21 months in federal prison. He had earlier faced state felony charges in Scott and New Madrid counties over the same conduct.
incident_date_approx: September 2023 - July 2024 (traffic stops; plaintiff's stop in Sikeston in April 2024)
description: A woman proceeding as Jane Doe filed a federal civil rights lawsuit on November 21, 2024 in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Missouri against former Missouri State Highway Patrol trooper David McKnight. The suit alleges that during an April 2024 traffic stop in Sikeston, McKnight unlawfully searched her phone to find and photograph nude images of her, violating her Fourth and Fourteenth Amendment rights; claims by additional women were later consolidated into the case, with the Highway Patrol also named. McKnight pleaded guilty in December 2025 to nine federal counts of deprivation of rights under color of law for searching nine women's phones for nude images during traffic stops, and in April 2026 he was sentenced to 21 months in prison. The consolidated civil case is set for a jury trial in September 2026.
notes: Per seed note: sexual misconduct/privacy violation rather than physical sexual assault. Consolidated individual filings (Doe 1 plus consolidated Jane Doe and Mary Roe claims) treated as one record; multiple_filings=true reflects the consolidation. A contemporaneous but separate case involving Florissant officer Julian Alcala (similar phone-search conduct) is a different agency and not part of this record.
inclusion_concern: Conduct at issue is sexual in nature (covert searches for and copying of nude images) and is central to the claims, but no physical sexual assault or harassment is alleged; flagging in case the database requires contact offenses or workplace harassment.
